answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. A new agent first publishes only a hash of its keypair, an opal that stays dull until lit, and must wait a full epoch before revealing it and transacting. Every later action is chained to that single thread, so a swarm of fresh identities cannot flare up and vanish like a comet: each one costs a locked deposit plus a visible waiting window, and clones that reveal identical behaviour are slashed together.
